Review: I was very disappointed with our stay here, my experience of the front desk staff was surprising, they were rude to me while we resolving an issue around our stay. The room was clean, nice amenities but it’s a large hotel and many rooms font have a good view.The staff in both the restaurant and the upstairs lounge were amazing though! Warm, fun and friendly. The food was excellent and the service was great. I will not return to this hotel next visit to Kathmandu. It’s very pretentious when it doesn’t need to be.

The wifi is not good at all especially in the 6th floor The food is average but good comparing to Kathmandu food quality.  The staff were nice and helped us in all requests but they need more training in the customer service   The location is good

Overall, the hotel is quite comfortable, with a full range of amenities,  and in a good location. However, their security was extremely slow to respond to a security incident at the hotel, leaving my colleagues and me feeling unsafe.

The staff & food were the best but the hotel itself is very old and unclean. Felth smell is very where. The internet is disconnected regularly.Nothing to do in surrounding area.Has 3 restaurants. I liked Indian and Chinese.

This hotel is majorly an expedition focused hotel…I was on a business trip and will not recommend business traveler to stay here. Have to move to other Marriott in city as the hotel approach is not good and the hotel is always full of travellers bags ( think they don’t have left luggage room). Which don’t give a great impression if you have a client visiting you.Hotel have one restaurant and it’s good, however guest are always recommended to go to the mall on which the hotel is located. Hotel have to work on training the staff  and process to run the hotel, as the other issue can’t be improved ( location) and its the most important one for any service to be successful.

Great resort type hotel but needs hotel staff improvement.  The staff do not greet their hotel guests and pool side food took awhile to arrive.    I traveled solo to Kathmandu to relax.  I was having a relaxing dinner and all of the sudden, a dozen of businessman marched in and were having a very loud business meeting.  After watching the meeting, I couldn't finish my meal and was very stressed out . Hyatt should of accommodated these people in a private room a removable partition walls/doors.
As a loyal customer and frequent guest this has been a very disappointing experience in terms of room preferences, room condition, cleanliness, and in terms of makingMe feel like a frequent customer.

Due to a conference presentation I am visiting this hotel.Since it is practical to stay at the conference venue I ask them to reserve a room for me .They called me up and informed me about an available room but when I went to register they said that room has been given another costumer who became sick!Good luck if you happen to stay here

Yes when you travel around Kathmandu the hotel looks impressive compared with the surroundings, however when the room is cooking in December and the solution by the engineer is turn off the AC and wait 30 mins you know that you are imposing first world complaints on a third world situation. Relax and sweat. Other than that. Bed is not great and I think I should have tried elsewhere.

I was supposed to spend a week here but fortunately only spent a night. My room was 407 and it looked onto a cinder block wall. To make matters worse I smelled smoke from the nearby buildings throughout the night. Yuck. As many other reviews have also noted the place is a bit run down. On the positive side, the staff are friendly, the grounds nice and the breakfast buffet good. The highlight was the Chimney Restaurant. They’ve recently changed the menu to “comfort food “ and I tried 3 different tapas and loved them. I’d give the restaurant 4-5 stars.

During dinner and starting at 9am there was some form of loud construction. The entire reason you go here is to be away from the city and for a peaceful area, this lack of foresight was unfortunate. ...

This hotel is closed and is not in existence any more. The profile of the hotel is existing on TA but the business is closed. I am writing this post for everyone information. I have discovered they are planning to build a large multiplex at this place.

This hotel is so out of Kathmandu city. Went there on a Saturday which is a public holiday with little traffic and by the time I reached the here I was already worried about returning back to the city. The pool is dirty and I the food is so oily and everything fried. The staff need training. Never recommending it to anyone or coming again. Stay away.

I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in Nov 2016.PRO's:Breakfast selections was very good and tasty.Staff were friendly and helpful.Indian restaurant was very good food and good service.CONS's:Room was very dated, I would imagine they have not been updated since the hotel was first built many many years ago.Bathroom was old and looked dirty/tatty - in real need of updating.Shower was in the bath.Chinese restaurant was very quiet, yet the service was incredibly slow, it took over one hour from our starter for them to bring out the main.The food overall was average at best, would not recommend trying this restaurant.Overall - I would not stay at this hotel again the price the hotel is too dated.

This hotel is built on the side of  steep hill and has a number of serious safety issues caused by the considerable number of stairways and passages in the building.Firstly, the electrical supply in Nepal is a bit unreliable so power outages are common.We were there for 2 nights and there were cuts on both of them. If you are in one of the bars or the restaurant the staff will set up battery powered lights but there is no backup lighting in any of the stairwells or corridors. When the power goes off these areas are left in total darkness. We raised this with the management and they seems unconcerned.Secondly, we identified at least one place in the hotel where it would be possible for smaller children to fall from one floor to the next.In addition to these concerns about safety we were also unimpressed with the level of service.The bedside light in our room didn't work and a maintenance person looked at them but couldn't fix them. On a couple of occasions, the staff were more interested in watching football on the TV than they were in serving the customers.This hotel is in a stunning location and with a bit of effort from the management it could be excellent, they need to get their act together.

The food was fine and the place is quite old. They also wanted to make us pay RS 2,000 for a guide on a paved path in the forest which is ridiculous for the amount we already pay per night. They REALLY need to update their gym.... the equipment is from the 80's. Not acceptable at a resort.

I cannot tell you how awful my experience was.  They spent 3hrs showing me deer and ignored me when I told them I have deer in my yard at home daily-I have actually wondered if they ignored my comments because I am a woman.  The jeep broke down 3 times-the driver was able to fix the battery and the fuel pump but the 3rd time he was stumped so we sat in the jungle 2 hrs waiting for another jeep when the guide had told me it would only take 30 min to walk out?  Needless to say when we finally got back at 7, I was too upset to do anything else and was thrilled to leave today.

Starting from lackadaisical staff at check in to no wi-fi service in the room, staff was not bothered about keeping the room clean or providing basic amenities like towels in the room. Even the staff at the restaurant for breakfast was non-responsive at all the occasions when approached.And was damn expensive for this kind of service and environment.

Mistic mountain Plus points Very beautifulAt top of hillAmazing view of HimalayasGood size roomsBeautiful roomsThey have Pool and JacuzziBut these  were not operational during our stay .no one informed us beforehand .Minus Poor availability of hot waterVery limited veg food options.v far from market so one is forced to eat hereToo overpriced for everything plus huge taxes Staff not v friendly .just doing their job no personal touch Spa overpriced underequipped Washroom has some wierd smell We chked in v late ( 5 hrs late )due to long drive and bad roads  . Were v tired .requested the manager for a room upgrade if possible but was denied.We were v tired. Tht night  our room 131 ac broke down znd threw up lots of water at 12 30 am soaking our bags and camera and mobile etc . No hot water at night .no hot water next morning too .so we complained.Finally we were given a new upgraded room ( too late )A gold facial cost 3000 plus almost 25 percent tax . Included just some v basic cream massage .and pack no steam Can avoid .Buffet lunch and dinner costs 1800 plus almost 25 percent  tax Overpriced for vegetarians atleast with very limited food choices.Food is understood bec the hotel is located atop hill so difficulty of supplies . But no hot water and staff indifference puts you off  for the rates they charge .

What I liked:- Good location, access to shops, restaurants outside the hotel- Attached casino- Overral service- great breakfast that was included with many choices- internet speed was decent, not fastIssues:- room is equivalent to a 3-star in Europe/US comparison but great overral- the pictures you see online for grand staircase and hallways are of the casino not hotel, hotel is a bit simpler- very busy hotel as tourists are there for Tibet tripWhat I didnt like is a bit of deceiving I got at dinner time. One of their restaurants was under construction, we didnt need much food just something small but they had only dinner buffet. I asked for price and they said Rs 1800 per person.  So I expected Rs 3600 for 2 people.  Its self service buffet. No other service was provided by the restaurant to us. When the bill came, not only is there a VAT of 13% but service charge of 10%.  It made the bill close to Rs 5000 as a bottle water was also charged because we didnt water regards water.  This is deceiving. When someone asks you a price, you should quote with service charge included and mention VAT is added otherwise, you are lying. And I have never seen service charge added for self service.  You should quote 2214 per person not 1800 because you know your charges. This way we can decide whether to eat there or go outside. So hope everyone from this review now knows the real buffet charge.

Breakfast and staff in breakfast areas are not up to 5 star standard. Manager and staff there are not welcoming, their rare smiles looked cold and forced. Food items were not fresh,  not replenished regularly and not kept hot. Croissants were stale and hard. Breakfast place is far from the rooms and problematic to reach when it rains. The shower head does not work well. TV worked half of the time and require hotel intervention every time which was annoying and time consuming. Decoration with photos of people who the hotel  has no idea about makes it look strange and more of an imitation than authentic about history or heritage.

We visited there with our big group 32 pax with 13 rooms reservation on 21 Sep 2019. Hotel property and view form the hotel is awesome . Staffs are nice and helpful . But I had very bad experience of slow check in service . We reached there by 3 Pm and we were checked in at the same time . But they gave us room almost 45 minutes late . I asked the check in guy about the problem . He said check out time is 12 noon and check in time at 2 Pm . But even at 3 Pm they dont have there room ready for us. Hope this type of service they should improve in future .

In this hotel usually started to use of energy specially bio gas (mithan gas) I don't know nowadays use or not! But leaknath district one of the 5 star hotel use of source of bio energy plant to cooking the food.

I spend 3 night in this hotel. I had a so much problem with wifi. It is so slow and not working. When I complain to front desk. They just say OK and never do anything. Other then wifi it was OK. This hotel has a free pic up service from or to airport.

Few minus but many plus.Check in should have been 2pm. But it was at 3pm.Reception staff requires much understanding. Specially the hotel gets in prime tourists.Room given in main building. It is very old, poor maint.and cries for much renovation. Poor bath room with leaking faucets. No electrical points for charging. Had to go down to request for extn.box . These are minus.of course they offered room in new wing but later. New wing in a different building. But it  is isolated and no life thete.Plus points and positives.Extremely good staff in restaurant , in the bar , house keeping. Very friendly and helpful. They make you feel welcome and makes up for all the other minus.Wish they keep the rooms renovated and the standards of Radisson kept up.

hotel is still impressive but food is somewhat disappointing especially outside of main restaurant (wasn't able to try Rox the other main restaurant as it's closed on Tuesdays).  Stayed in part of the Presidential Suite (701) which was very impressive with huge balcony.  Stayed at hotel 7 yrs ago and it seems about the same.  Prices are more than double of 4 or 5 star properties especially in Pokhara.  However, the spa was less than half the price of the Marriott's spa.   It's a good choice for  a couple or few nights max.  Location not as central as others but transportation is cheap although traffic terrible.

I spent two nights at the Yak & Yeti in October 2017. Overall, it was a good stay but not without some issues.Positives:-Airport pick-up and communication before my arrival was very good-Checking in was fast and good-Room was ok, not bad but not really 5 star quality. Especially for the prices they charge. It needs a refurb, the room, bathroom, new TV etc.-Location of the hotel is very good, central, taxi drivers knows the hotel which helps-Staff was generally good, helpful, polite-Breakfast options were reasonableNegatives:-As I said earlier, staff was generally good but there is one elder gentleman behind reception who talks to you without looking at you which is a bit strange/rude. The younger guys and girls were all good.-Like I said earlier, the room I was in, can do with a refurb, especially for the prices they charge-I had arranged and confirmed an airport drop-off but it turned out the relevant people who had to book the car weren't aware, so there was some minor delay.Like I said, all in all, a good stay and I would definitely consider staying here again if I were to return to Kathmandu.

Main reason for the rating is the location and views. I was very lucky with my room (it did come at a cost) with subbing views of the lake and the mountains.Reason for not giving it a higher score is that the hotel is very dated, seems to have been massive at a time and it hasn’t kept up to date with many thingsBathroom wasn’t nice for a £200+ stay and something as basic as no light in my night table .. I had to stand up to switch off the lightsStaff were very nice on arrival but on departure they couldn’t have been less helpful. Receptionist was not helpful when the card reader wasn’t working and she kept blaming it on my card - it was their problem in the end. Finally when I was leaving (went back to pick bags), receptionist was rude, and wouldn’t help. There is a lovely person helping tourists with bookings (sorted my bus tickets to Kathmandu) and he booked me a cab for a fraction of what the receptionist wanted me to pay

We stayed in the older part which is a bit dated.Rooms have old furniture but comfy bed.Tv remote had no off button.  Air con worked well.Like most hotel rooms, not enough lights.Our room had a connecting door, which I think was made out of cardboard - could hear everything.Restaurant was first class.  Plenty of choice.

This is the 4th time I am staying in radisson however I had opportunity to write the review this time only . The review is as follows Rooms - rooms are big , clean , good wifi connectivity , nice ambience and clean beds . Toilets - toilets are very clean and neat and well maintained Room service - room service is pretty good and fast . The choice of veg is less and you have plenty of non veg options . Truly international and prefer to order non veg in room service . Inspite I have ordered veg thali ( Indian meal ) in the night and it Islas good for a place like Kathmandu . No complains .Restaurant - coffee shop - the coffee shop is in the 3rd floor and they serve breakfast in the morning . Good one to visit Traveldesk - poor one and lot of service improvement is needed . Inspite of prior information the communication does not go properly from the reception and they fumble lot to give a decent pickup from airport . The quality of vehicles are pretty ordinary one and you don't feel like travelling in the same when you land . Radisson has to seriously to change the vehicle fleet which gives a bad impression . Swimming pool and gym - thete is a pool and gym in the 5th floor in old building and it is open always . Okay not highly impressive and it is crowded Spa - it is in the -1 level in new building and I had 15 min head massage for 1 day . Okay one not too impressive . Overall the Experience is like a normal hotel nothing too good and impressive to pull international traveller.

Its good to stay but staff attitude in fun café is not appreciable. They are very lethargic and many time service is not rendered and you leave place without even completed food .  I guess the staff is not well trained about how they should behave in hospitality industry

Some of Kathmandu's five star hotels have legal casinos in their premises. But the casino establishments are owned and operated by third parties, and not by the five star hotels themselves. A unique feature of these casinos is that Nepal's citizens are not allowed to gamble here

After arriving into Kathmandu, with my luggage still sitting in Doha, I made my way to an AirBnB that I had booked. Exhausted and desperately needing a shower, I decided to nap first, but just as I collapsed onto the bed, I saw bugs crawling on the sheets. I knew I could not stay there another minute, let alone two weeks. Realizing I needed to upscale, I chose Crown Plaza Soaltee. The warmth of their greeting upon my arrival was unrivaled. Muna, the Duty Manager, was a godsend. Everything I needed, Muna provided for me. First and foremost, I needed my luggage. Muna said that the Crown Plaza airport representative could collect it from the airport and bring it to my room on their next run to the airport. I needed a SIM card and Muna said the gift store could provide me with one. Muna even copied my passport, which is required to obtain a SIM card. As part of the hotel policy, the Crown Plaza Soaltee provides single women with rooms closest to the elevator and they do not release the room number to anyone. Having traveled to many cities in many countries, I have stayed at many hotels. I can honestly say that the Soaltee, mostly due to Muna, offers the best customer service that I have ever received.

This is a lovely hotel in a very poor country which lacks the basic infrastructure we westerners take for granted.  Pick up from the airport is a battle but nothing to what the locals get.  On arrival we were greeted by staff who dealt with our luggage and offered a cold drink and chocolates.  The desk staff are very competent, polite and speak English perfectly.  Our rooms were delightful and beautifully decorated though the cupboard space is not so good.  Our shower outlet overflowed but the next one outside the shower dealt with the water.  One day a man and woman asked to come in to wash the windows.  He scraped the ledge with a screw driver, she wiped the windows with a dry cloth.  They left after two minutes the windows just as dirty as when the came in!   We felt like fat indulgent westerners in a country where everything is done manually, by people who have no training and earn a pittance.  How could we complain.A strip of cute small shops lines the corridor to the conference centre.  Don't go near them.  You will be harangued for an hour to buy stuff you were never interested in.The staff all over this hotel were very polite and hard working and keen to please, the young bar staff with their limited English put up with all sorts of difficult western requests with humour and professionalism and a keenness to please.  Paper delivery was intermittent and when I asked "Staff Services" about my paper she rudely told me to go and read it in the business centre.  When I asked a very un-busy "Travel Services" woman about where I could do a cookery course she said she didn't know in a very uninterested way.  Go to the Tamal she suggested.  I found one on line.We ate most meals in the hotel as they were fantastic and offered great banquets and a la carte.  Plenty, delicious, and varied.  Chefs cook select dishes at most meals.  Waffles with real maple syrup, can you believe it! The coffee could be better, another western cry, but hey, this is Nepal!  They do fantastic masala tea everywhere.Another western complaint.....the air conditioning was not connected to the control.  Just open the window.Overall great comfortable, lovely staff, centrally located.....

The Glacier hotel is a great place in Pokhara. Right next to the lake. Central location, on the main road with several shops, bars and restaurants around and a very short walk to the center of Pokhara. The rooms are Splendid, beds are super comfortable, water is hot, heaters work well, the decor of the whole hotel makes it clear that attention to the very small details was taken into consideration whilst furnishing and decorating the place. The restaurant on the ground Floor 'Harbor' is excellent, the service was amazing and the food was the best we've had in Nepal. Breakfast was varied and the restaurant staff are very friendly and professional. The owner was always hanging out around the place mingling with customers asking them about their experience. We were there for new Year and they organized a free trip to a mountain top to watch the sunrise on the 1st of Jan, 2017 - we couldn't make it as it was too early to wake up after NY party but it was a nice touch as the owner sent a private letter to each room inviting everyone and he joined the tour. The most annoying thing about this place is the WIFI. This is coming from a person who doesn't usually give much importance to Wifi and doesn't mind 'not being connected' however - if the place advertises that they don't have wifi it would be better coz then you'd know what to expect. You can never connect, then if you accidentally got lucky, if you move from one page to the other - you would need to re-enter the password and username - every time. It's very frustrating if you need to plan your next move, look at reviews for day trips, flights or anything really. I am aware that the internet connection across all Nepal is not that great but we had better wifi in bars and in other hotels in Pokhara and Kathmandu. For a hotel that costs you about 120$ a night - this is unacceptable. The reception staff's reply was that 'the doors are too thick' :) The other thing that was a let down was the half day tour organized by the hotel, they informed us that a full day trip is 90$ and a half day tour is 50$ - when we asked to alter the tour meaning 'removed 3 of the spots they recommended and asked to visit one other spot instead' they charged us 70$. I didn't think it was fair but well we didn't argue. The half day trip was a disaster, the car broke down and we had to wait for another car to come. After driving for about 1.5 hrs it turned out that the road was blocked and had to drive for 2 hrs straight back again... basically the day was a waste of time sitting in a car and seeing only a pagoda and a bridge in the span of 6 hours for 70$ - when i tried to explain to the receptionist that it wasn't a fair price she gave me an attitude and said she will check with her manager - then they still charged me the same price plus extra fees as i paid by debit card instead of cash.

I stayed here for 1 night before my Himalaya trek and 2 nights after my trek. Good guest rooms and grounds. Very good breakfast. However, I was surprised that a hotel of this standard charges its guests for Wi-Fi. Also, as I booked this hotel as part of a package, the gym facilities were not included. This is very poor practice and does not promote the hotel in a positive way.

One of the oldest hotels in Kathmandu, Annapurna delivers all the basics of a 5 star hotel and leaves no room for complaints. Does it leave an impression or is there an extra ordinary service or incident to recall and cherish ? - No. Another good hotel like in any other city.!!

Cozy rooms, I was impressed with the pleasant smell, everything is spotless including the toilet,prices adjusted to the luxury offered by this hotel, you can not ask for more,It was nice staff who tried in all ways to make us feel at ease recommended

where in the world can you find a hotel where the OLD WING is in better condition than the NEW WING? I have to say that when we/ I stay at the Radisson I insist on the old building. its old but it is solid and has character unlike the new wing which was built on the cheap and the rooms now reflect that lack of extra care and cashDon't get me wrong I really like the Radisson and its characterBUT! my wife sent her lovely expensive slacks to be dry cleaned and laundered. it was supposed to be 24hr service. . Anyway after 3 days of chasing making a bit of a ruckus at reception we finally got a knock at the door. It was the laundry manager and the Rooms Division Manager. Yeap you guessed it, they made a mistake and my Wife's white slacks now had turned into light blue. whoops!The annoying thing was that if they had fessed up straight away we could have accepted it better. 3 days of dodge and weave made us a little angry!YOU WANT SERVICE? YOU WANT CUSTOMER SATISFACTION? YOU WANT TO BE AMAZED?After discussions about what we can do to resolve this issue, they finally asked us to come to reception. They had scoured Kathmandu to try and find a similar pair off slacks. Then with 2 managers a driver and a car they took my wife shopping for a pair of slacks in the western shops of Kathmandu. unfortunately they had nothing to which compared.(read this again 3 staff a car and 2 customers for 2 hours)A compensation figure was negotiated (one of those chq's in the mail scenarios, you know the one)LESS than a week of arriving home I had received a chq in the mail from World Expeditions for the nominated amount.all this was organised via the Radisson hotel.There, I rest my case! why stay anywhere else thanks to Deepak Man Pradhan, Subash Khadka at the Radisson and Emma from World Ex in SydneyReally impressed, I'm still in awe of this service

It is one hour away from Pokhara Airport but the shuttle service provided by resort made our journey shorter. Very comfortable bed with a wide room, buffet dinner, and breakfast with a variety of dishes.  Friendly waiters and waitresses were available all the time. Bishal was very amiable. The Sauna was perfect. Steam was OK, as the temperature of the steam room was not hot enough. Very surprisingly none of the staff offered or had tea or coffee during breakfast. When we ordered coffee, they charged extra. As a star hotel please provide coffee during breakfast or let your guests know that they get tea/coffee in the morning included in the package so that they don't need to order the chargeable tea/coffee.

I was there about a month ago on an organised tour and this hotel was one of the best we stayed at.  I was actually not very well and the waiter noticed I hadn't finished my soup and asked if everything was all right.  When I told him I wasn't well he insisted I chose something different, some plain rice for example, and offered to have it sent to my room.  You couldn't ask for better/kinder service than that!  All the staff was helpful and friendly, the rooms first class and the food very good.

We visited the hotel when our helicopter landed here to get refuelled.The views of Mount Everest were breathtaking. The weather was perfect for scenic photos that day. We ordered ginger lemon honey tea but were told there were no lemons that day. We also ordered a serve of fries and they came after some time but were piping hot and delicious.The hotel itself was very cold inside. We wanted to borrow the restroom but decided not to after seeing it was outside in the cold.
